sections.overview: The nine-banded armadillo is a widespread American mammal that has expanded northward in the United States in recent decades.
sections.identification: Its bony armor has nine flexible bands between the shoulder and rump shields, plus a long ringed tail.
sections.habitat: It favors soils that are easy to dig and uses stream banks, grasslands and woodland edges for burrows and foraging.
sections.diet: Its broad diet is mainly insects and other invertebrates, with occasional small vertebrates, fruit and fungi.
sections.behavior: It is mostly active in the evening and at night in warm weather, and probes soil for prey.
sections.reproduction: A single fertilized ovum usually produces four genetically identical young after delayed implantation.
sections.ecology: Its digging and insect-rich diet link it closely to soil texture, ground invertebrates and riparian corridors.
sections.conservation: The 2013 global IUCN assessment lists it as Least Concern, based on its broad range and adaptability.
